## What has been tried

Newest first. The `why` is the part that will still be worth reading later.

**2026-08-24T20:36:50Z** — a false disk alarm caused by the rotation itself · *MEASURED*

- config: `samples now carry their writing node; the disk trend compares within one box only, and needs a 30-minute window before it will extrapolate`
- produced: the alarm cleared; 119 tests pass; selftest still fires all 10 alarms
- why: The alarm was right that free space had dropped by 850 GB and wrong that anything was filling: it compared two different machines. Worth recording because the general shape bites any long-haul metric — most of them are about the RUN and survive a box change, and the few that are about the MACHINE do not. A false critical on a routine event is how an alarm gets ignored, so it earned a fix and not a threshold.
- control: two suppression tests (a rotation, a bootstrap) plus a test requiring a genuine one-box slope AND the free-space cliff to still fire — suppressions without that third test would be indistinguishable from switching the alarm off

**2026-08-24T20:34:25Z** — the first unplanned box rotation, end to end · *MEASURED*

- config: `117796's lease reclaimed at 20:30Z with no stand-down; fresh box 42504 provisioned, bootstrapped from the repo, recovered, dead box retired, supervisor restarted`
- produced: clone+build 5.2s; recover found 47 files identical between the GitHub clone and the paste mirror; the worker resumed at resume_evals=1068 read out of the repo; the budget did NOT re-count the resume point; the new supervisor banked and pushed 6a38e0f0 on its own with no proxy in its environment; all alarms clear
- why: This is the rotation the whole harness exists for, and it happened for real rather than as a drill: the lease went away underneath a running supervisor. Everything held except two things worth having found — a vanished box could not be retired at all, and the bridge credential has to be re-copied to each new box.
- control: tmhaul beat, run on the fresh box before any intervention, said exactly 'the run belongs to a box that is gone; take it over here' and exited 3 — the diagnosis came from committed state, since that box had never seen this project

**2026-08-24T20:05:00Z** — a silent fetch failure that made the retry loop lie · *MEASURED*

- config: `sync_with_remote returned Ok(None) on a failed git fetch; git network calls now go through gitcmd::git_env, which supplies the forward proxy unless the environment already sets one; rebase uses --autostash`
- produced: a full bank under 'env -u https_proxy -u http_proxy' now commits, mirrors and pushes; origin/main == local HEAD at 3e3f22b3, with both other sessions' commits (992c438, 5fa72b8) ancestors of ours
- why: This is the project's signature bug INSIDE the harness written to catch it, and my retry loop turned a silent no-op into a confident false explanation — worse than the original failure, because it named a cause. Two lessons: a fetch that could not run is UNKNOWN and never 'nothing to do'; and a detached process inherits nothing, so any dependency on an exported variable works interactively and fails unattended.
- control: the negative arm is the run itself: stripping every proxy variable from the environment is the condition that used to fail silently, and it now succeeds. Before the fix the same command reported 'the remote kept moving' three times against a remote that had not moved

**2026-08-24T19:59:24Z** — push retry under a moving remote · *MEASURED*

- config: `both push routes retry up to 3 times, re-syncing each round`
- produced: the bank that had failed went through; origin/main and local HEAD agree
- why: The first rebase fix closed the case where the remote had already moved. It could not close the window between our fetch and our push, which is where the second failure landed. Two unrelated sessions pushed to this repo in the harness's first hour, so the window is not theoretical.
- control: a test builds a bare origin and two clones, syncs, THEN lands the other clone's commit, and requires the push to still land and both pieces of work to survive — a single-shot push fails that test

**2026-08-24T19:57:12Z** — correcting an independence claim I made about the start line · *SUPERSEDED*

- config: `the start-position check compares against the map's DECLARED Spawn waypoint`
- produced: the code comment, HARNESS.md and this ledger now say ONE source
- why: I wrote that the map's Spawn cell and the lead's 3D render independently agreed on (1584, 784). They do not: the render showed the route mesh and the suspect trajectory and never identified the start line. Two readings that share a source prove nothing, and I asserted corroboration that did not exist while writing a check whose entire purpose is catching that class of error. An independent second source means reading tick 0 out of a live re-simulation, which is what G2 now requires of a driving worker.
- control: none — this is a retraction, and it is recorded because the corrected version is weaker than what I reported

**2026-08-24T19:57:12Z** — the four acceptance gates · *MEASURED*

- config: `tmhaul claim, the only route from a worker's output to banked state: G1 reproducible (frame + prefix + map/template/tape hashes), G2 live tick 0 for a driving worker, G3 fail closed with no start control, G4 the oracle's raw transcript banked beside the claim`
- produced: a claim of the shape the explorer currently produces is refused by all four; a complete one is accepted and banks every hash, the frame, the prefix or the word root, tick 0 and the transcript's md5
- why: The explorer's five confirmed tapes could not be reproduced: wrong start position or a state locator on the wrong object, and no replay frame. The lead held integration back, correctly. What generalises is not a fix to that explorer but the standard every worker must meet — a tape nobody can re-derive is not a result, and an unchecked start is not a passing one.
- control: tmhaul gates walks seven broken claims and one good one — each breaks exactly ONE field of the same complete claim, so a test can only pass by exercising the gate it names, and the good claim must be accepted. A test asserts --no-drive exempts G2 and nothing else, so the flag cannot become a way to switch the gates off

**2026-08-24T19:48:07Z** — the first full standing re-simulation sweep · *MEASURED*

- config: `tmresim over all 36 map dirs, plain oracle in process, one server launch per map, against a 94-row map registry`
- produced: 174 tapes in 3m: 112 hold, 0 differ, 1 DNF (a file named DO_NOT_PUBLISH, declaring 40.226, doing DNF cp5), 1 STARTED-ELSEWHERE (magnet trial's CUT tape, 1089.2 m out), 13 refused as human, 47 UNMEASURED
- why: The rule that every banked result is re-simulated STANDING has been in RULES.md all along with nothing performing it. The valuable output is not the 112: it is the 47. Better than a quarter of the corpus cannot be placed by provenance, so it is not covered — and the fix is the PROV record, not a wider list of filename prefixes, because guessing that best_* is probably ours is exactly the reasoning that leaks a ghost.
- control: 0 differ across 112 tapes is the claim; the DNF row is the control that the detector can say no, since that file was already known to declare a time it does not achieve. The start check is separately two-sided: 10.6 m on a real tape at a 0.001 m tolerance, silent at 32 m

**2026-08-24T19:19:37Z** — two harness bugs found by running it, not by reading it · *MEASURED*

- config: `supervisor eval baseline seeded from the repo; watch refuses to start beside a live supervisor; budget gains an append-only correction record`
- produced: the budget read 582 evals for 308 done and now reads 308; a second supervisor is refused by name and pid instead of silently coexisting
- why: Both bugs are invisible to a reading and obvious within twenty minutes of running. The budget one is the more serious: it inflates in the direction of switching to a learned ordering too early, and it does so precisely because restart-and-resume is the system's NORMAL mode rather than an exception. Worth remembering that the harness's own instruments need the same suspicion as the project's.
- control: the seeding test asserts 194 from a repo that says 194 AND zero from an empty repo — a seeder that always returns the last number it saw would pass only the first half; the correction test asserts the log still has three lines, so nothing was rewritten

- produced: it ran normally for 60 s, entered the lead window at exactly expiry-minus-30m, stopped the worker, banked, verified every file's md5 against the commit, and retired the box in the registry
- why: The unit test covers the decision; this covers the plumbing, and they are different claims. The 18-hour lease cap makes this the most-used path in the whole system over a month, and it is the one path where getting it wrong destroys a box's work rather than merely stopping it.

**2026-08-24T19:08:37Z** — banking through a third-party push to main · *MEASURED*

- config: `bank now runs git fetch + rebase when the branch has diverged, retries the push, and forces only the render box's scratch ref`
- produced: origin/main == local HEAD at 6e113c1e, with the other session's 992c438 an ancestor of ours; three banks in a row before the fix recorded PUSH FAILED while the mirror kept succeeding
- why: This repo is not ours alone and a months-long system must survive its colleagues. The failure was also instructive about layering: the mirror and the push have no credential, service or machine in common, which is exactly why one kept working while the other was broken for twelve minutes.

**2026-08-24T19:01:04Z** — the recovery demonstration: kill -9 mid-flight, wipe the box, continue from the repo · *MEASURED*

- config: `kill -9 on supervisor and worker (no run_stop, no final bank), rm -rf the checkout and the harness state on the box, then a clean clone + build + tmhaul recover + tmhaul watch --detach`
- produced: detected from the repo alone as CRITICAL zero_throughput 12m after the last sample; recovered with resume_evals=80 read out of the repo; throughput resumed 80 -> 160 -> 189 evals and every alarm cleared. Cost of the crash: 34 evals, about 90 seconds. Clone 3.8 s, build 4.9 s.
- why: This is the deliverable that proves the rest. Durability claims are cheap to write and this project has been burned by exactly that; the only convincing form is to destroy the box and show the work continue. It also produced the honest bound: a crash costs at most one banking window of RECORD, and artifacts survive only if the worker writes them into state/frontier -- which the rung-1 explorer will have to do and the sweep did not need to.
- control: the same fresh checkout, 1m34s after the kill, fired NOTHING — so the alarm is capable of silence, which is the half that makes the firing mean something. And the mirror's 17 files came back byte-identical to the clone's: two transports (GitHub via a deploy key on Windows, a paste via x509) with nothing in common, agreeing.

**2026-08-24T18:44:33Z** — the standing re-simulation sweep as the harness's first real workload · *MEASURED*

- config: `tmresim --loop --pause-s 300, plain oracle in process via ghost::oracle::validate_many, batched one server launch per map`
- produced: 7 of 7 tapes on Kacky Reloaded #290 re-simulated at exactly their published times in 6 s; the full sweep is 174 tapes across 36 maps
- why: The project's rule is that a banked result is re-simulated by the plain oracle standing, not as a spot check — and until now nothing made that true. It is also the right first job for the harness: hours long, countable, real failure modes, and it reads a corpus that is NOT in the repo, which is what surfaced the one real gap in the recovery story.
- control: the no-ghost gate is two-sided and tested: a human recording is refused, one of our own tapes is accepted, and a file nothing places is refused rather than assumed ours

**2026-08-24T18:44:33Z** — the long-haul harness itself · *MEASURED*

- config: `tmhaul: repo-as-state-of-record, detached supervisor, cron heartbeat, 8 alarms, work-counting budget; tmresim as the first worker`
- produced: 86 + 12 tests green; every alarm fired from a fixture and against a live process; a full bank does commit + paste mirror + GitHub push in about 70 s
- why: Every failure the project hit on 2026-08-24 was a durability failure, not an algorithm failure. The five were: a supervising agent settling while its child ran; a stall detector that could not fire at zero evals; the 18-hour lease cap; a 30-day store used as a months-long one; and a budget clock burning during a stall. Each is answered by a mechanism rather than a note in a document, because a note does not fire at 3am.
- control: alarms selftest pairs each alarm with a state that must fire it AND a healthy control that must fire nothing; live-test runs four real workers (normal, stall, crash, silent) and reads the firings back off disk
